# n11 - What the meld broke and what it half-closed

v2 re-verified the n9 and n10 meld at `resources/review--v2-meld-2026-09-11.md`. All four of v1's
blockers are genuinely closed, hand-reproduced against a real repository. The meld itself opened two
new blockers and five new majors, and left three of v1's findings closed only in the shape their
test exercises.

The pattern is worth naming before the work starts: every one of the new defects is on a path the
meld created. B1's fix writes the executor's own prose into a ledger field, and the ledger refuses a
newline. M4's fix wired proposals into absorb, and the proposal path re-enters the graph loader
unguarded. M12's fix wrapped an atomic rewrite in a lock that the rewrite's own rename defeats. New
production surface written in one pass carries new failure modes, and this node closes them.

Two of them let the runner write `done` on work nothing verified, which is the one thing this
intent exists to prevent, so they lead.

## n11 failure-mode matrix
| Row | Operation | Failure mode | Test |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 11.1 | Normalize a return's `question:` and `reason:` before writing them into a ledger field (v2 NEW-1) | `NodeLedger.normalize_value` raises on a tab or a newline, so a two-line question crashes `runner step` with a raw trace, writes no transition, leaves the node `running`, and skips every later phase of the step | `runner_absorb_test#test_multiline_question_is_normalized_into_one_field` |
| 11.2 | Write a transition even when the return's prose cannot be normalized at all (v2 NEW-1) | A pathological return silently costs the whole step and the node is stuck `running` until its lease expires | `runner_absorb_test#test_unwritable_return_prose_blocks_rather_than_raises` |
| 11.3 | Refuse the absorb when `context.graph[:ok]` is false or the node's kind is not declared (v2 NEW-2) | `kind` is nil, the work branch is skipped, no merge runs, `declared_files` is empty so scope passes vacuously, and `done` is written with the executor's self-reported commit on work that never reached the intent branch | `runner_absorb_test#test_unresolvable_kind_blocks_rather_than_writing_done` |
| 11.4 | Prove the unmerged `done` cannot be written, against a real branch (v2 NEW-2) | The fix is asserted against a fixture and a real return still lands a `done` whose commit is not an ancestor of the intent branch | `runner_absorb_test#test_done_requires_the_commit_to_be_merged` |
| 11.5 | Record `suite:unreadable` rather than `suite` in `gates=` on the `verify_command_unreadable` state (v2 NEW-3) | M2's defect returns on the state M1 added: the evidence field claims a suite that never ran | `runner_absorb_test#test_gates_says_suite_unreadable_on_that_state` |
| 11.6 | Stop claiming a guard the code does not have when appending a finding (v2 NEW-4) | `GuardedAppend` holds one open handle and `AtomicWrite` renames a new inode over the path, so a second writer takes the lock on an unlinked inode and loses its line while being told it was written | `runner_absorb_test#test_finding_append_does_not_claim_a_guard_it_lacks` |
| 11.7 | Keep the finding append atomic and newline-correct without the false guard (v2 NEW-4) | Dropping the guard drops the atomicity with it and a crash mid-write truncates the intent record | `runner_absorb_test#test_finding_append_stays_atomic` |
| 11.8 | Guard `RunnerProposals`' own graph load and validate calls (v2 NEW-5) | M4 made this path reachable from absorb, so a `--return` carrying a proposal dies with a raw trace on a malformed `graph.md` | `runner_absorb_test#test_proposal_path_refuses_a_malformed_graph_without_raising` |
| 11.9 | Guard the `render_status` call inside the absorb (v2 NEW-5) | A `--return` on a running node writes its transition and then dies with a raw trace, so the step ends half done | `runner_cli_test#test_return_on_a_running_node_survives_a_malformed_graph` |
| 11.10 | Let `runner answer` unpark a `blocked` node (v2 NEW-6) | `blocked` is in neither `READY_PRIOR_STATES` nor `TERMINAL_STATES`, so a node that blocks is dead forever, and the meld made `blocked` reachable by executor choice and by a broken project record | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_unparks_a_blocked_node` |
| 11.11 | Refuse to unpark a node that is not parked at all (v2 NEW-6) | Widening `answer` to `blocked` widens it to everything and a healthy node can be hand-released with no evidence | `runner_answer_test#test_answer_still_refuses_a_healthy_node` |
| 11.12 | Report `queued` whenever any node is running, not only when a ready node finds no slots (v2 NEW-7) | The ordinary in-flight case, every ready node already running, falls through to `stalled`, so the operator reads a busy graph as a dead one | `runner_dispatch_test#test_running_nodes_report_queued_not_stalled` |
| 11.13 | Report a refused proposal's validator verdict at the absorb (v2 minor 8) | An accepted proposal that invalidates the graph is written, unreported, and bricks every later step with `invalid_graph` | `runner_absorb_test#test_proposal_validator_verdict_is_reported` |
| 11.14 | Apply a proposal only on a return that says `done` (v2 minor 11) | An executor looping on retries grows the graph on every failed attempt | `runner_absorb_test#test_proposals_are_not_applied_on_a_failing_return` |
| 11.15 | Treat a `project.yml` that parses to a non-Hash as unreadable, not absent (v2 minor 13) | M1 is half-closed on its own stated intent: only a raise blocks, so a malformed-but-parsable record still lands `done` with `suite:absent` | `runner_absorb_test#test_non_hash_project_record_is_unreadable` |
| 11.16 | Rescue the digest when hashing an unreadable file (v1 minor 6, dropped by n10) | `Digest::SHA256.file` raises `Errno::EACCES` and `CoreIntegrity` breaks its own never-raises contract | `core_integrity_test#test_unreadable_file_is_reported_not_raised` |
| 11.17 | Read the suite counts from the last summary line, not the first match (v1 minor 7, dropped by n10) | A suite that exits zero with an earlier red sub-process summary records the wrong counts on the `done` line | `runner_absorb_test#test_suite_counts_come_from_the_last_summary` |
| 11.18 | Print the merge-in-progress warning once (v1 minor 3, dropped by n10) | The library and the CLI both warn and the operator reads the same sentence twice | `runner_cli_test#test_merge_warning_is_printed_once` |

## Steps
1. Red: the matrix's tests above, committed before any code.
2. Fix the two blockers first, then the five majors, then the rest.
3. Green, then the whole suite at its baseline.
